key_insight: AI/ML methods are essential to extract robust dark‑energy and dark‑matter constraints from LSST's unprecedented, heterogeneous data; targeted investments in scalable, uncertainty‑aware, and operationally robust ML will unlock LSST's scientific potential.
problem_solved: Addresses how to analyze extremely large, heterogeneous LSST datasets (images, catalogs, alerts) while controlling statistical and systematic uncertainties, meeting scalability and real‑time operational requirements for cosmological inference.
method: Survey and prioritize AI/ML opportunities (classification, anomaly detection, simulation‑based inference, surrogate modeling, domain adaptation) aligned to DESC science goals.
Advocate practical research & engineering: uncertainty quantification, interpretability, robust calibration with simulated training data, benchmarking and reproducible pipelines.
Design deployment pathways: scalable compute, real‑time alert integration, end‑to‑end validation from simulated training to cosmological parameter estimation.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a roadmap of high‑impact, real‑world problems with abundant simulated and observational data, clear benchmarking needs, and requirements for scalable, uncertainty‑aware models that will be deployed in production astrophysics pipelines.
visual_elements: Data flow funnel: LSST inputs (images, catalogs, alerts) → ML modules (classification, denoising, inference) → cosmological parameters (dark energy constraints).
Bar/area chart comparing data volume and compute requirements vs capabilities of traditional pipelines to highlight scalability needs.
Matrix/heatmap mapping AI techniques (e.g., domain adaptation, SBI, uncertainty quantification) to specific DESC science tasks.
Pipeline diagram showing training on realistic simulations → transfer/robustification → real‑time alert processing → end‑to‑end validation and cosmological analysis.
paper_title: Opportunities in AI/ML for the Rubin LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
paper_authors: LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration, Eric Aubourg, Camille Avestruz, Matthew R. Becker, Biswajit Biswas
